issue.title: Enhancement: watchdog API implementation for Nexthop devices

failure.body:
### Is it platform specific

broadcom

### Importance or Severity

Medium

### Description of the enhancement

To support arming the watchdog via a persistent "watchdog puncher" service while also allowing for manual override calls.

### Current Behavior

- No support of watchdog puncher by software
- The Watchdog API cannot distinguish between an arming request from a watchdog puncher and an explicit manual arm. Consequently, a manual arm may be inadvertently overridden by the watchdog puncher.

**Example Scenario:** Assume a device has watchdog puncher software that arms the watchdog every 10 seconds. If a user manually arms the watchdog using `watchdogutil arm -s 20` (setting it to 20 seconds) but does not call `watchdogutil disarm`, the device will never reboot or power cycle. This is because the watchdog puncher will re-arm the watchdog within 10 seconds, effectively nullifying the user's manual timer.

### Proposed Behavior

- Separate code paths to allow watchdog puncher to re-arm the watchdog and explicit, manual arm
- Add a watchdog puncher (a systemd service and timer to arm watchdog using `watchdogutil`. Install and enable the timer. Every minute, the FPGA watchdog is armed (punched) with 3 minutes

Create a dedicated API for use by only watchdog puncher. For other explicit arming (by `watchdogutil arm` call, for example), create a watchdog pause file `/var/lock/pddf-locks/watchdog.pause`. While the pause file is present, the watchdog punching will have no effect.

**Example Scenario (Revised):** Assume the device has a watchdog puncher arming the watchdog every 10 seconds. If a user arms the watchdog manually with `watchdogutil arm -s 20`, the puncher is paused. If the user does not call `watchdogutil disarm`, the device will successfully reboot or power cycle after approximately `20` seconds as intended.

resolution.title: [Nexthop] Improve Nexthop watchdog support
resolution.description:
#### Why I did it

Fixes #25222

- Please ignore commits like `IGNORE THIS COMMIT: Refactor unit tests for sonic-platform-modules-nexthop (PR #25166)`
- To add a persistent software watchdog puncher
- To support arming the watchdog via a persistent "watchdog puncher" service while also allowing for manual `arm` calls.

##### Work item tracking
- Microsoft ADO **(number only)**:

#### How I did it
- Add a separate API `arm_from_daemon()` for exclusive use by watchdog puncher
- Create a pause file `/var/lock/pddf-locks/watchdog.pause` when a manual `arm` has been called
- Remove the pause file when `disarm` is called. `/var/lock/pddf-locks/watchdog.pause` is ideal because it is not persistent across reboot. The path is also mounted on pmon so that it is accessible in sonic-mgmt testing.
- Add a systemd watchdog puncher on Nexthop devices
- Add `override.conf` to disable `watchdog-control.service`, so that FPGA watchdog is enabled permanently

#### How to verify it

- Unit tests
- [sonic-mgmt test](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/blob/master/tests/platform_tests/api/test_watchdog.py)

 ```
$ sudo systemctl list-timers watchdog
NEXT                        LEFT LAST                         PASSED UNIT           ACTIVATES
Wed 2026-01-28 <IPV6> UTC  12s Wed 2026-01-28 <IPV6> UTC 47s ago watchdog.timer watchdog.service

1 timers listed.
Pass --all to see loaded but inactive timers, too.
$ sudo python -c "import sonic_platform; print(sonic_platform.platform.Platform().get_chassis().get_watchdog().get_remaining_time())"
359
```

Wait for the next run.

```
$ sudo systemctl list-timers watchdog
NEXT                        LEFT LAST                         PASSED UNIT           ACTIVATES
Wed 2026-01-28 <IPV6> UTC   6s Wed 2026-01-28 <IPV6> UTC 53s ago watchdog.timer watchdog.service

1 timers listed.
Pass --all to see loaded but inactive timers, too.

$ sudo python -c "import sonic_platform; print(sonic_platform.platform.Platform().get_chassis().get_watchdog().get_remaining_time())"
357
```

Stop the watchdog.timer. System should powercycle eventually

```
$ sudo systemctl stop watchdog.timer
```

Lock file is created after `watchdogutil arm`
```
$ sudo watchdogutil status
Status: Armed
Time remaining: 323 seconds

$ sudo ls -l /var/lock/pddf-locks/watchdog.pause
ls: cannot access '/var/lock/pddf-locks/watchdog.pause': No such file or directory

$ date +%s; sudo watchdogutil arm -s 100
1769629448
Watchdog armed for 100 seconds

$ sudo ls -l /var/lock/pddf-locks/watchdog.pause
-rw-r--r-- 1 root root 10 Jan 28 19:42 /var/lock/pddf-locks/watchdog.pause
```

Watchdog is still armed after 60 seconds (punch frequency)

```
$ date +%s; sudo watchdogutil status
1769629510
Status: Armed
Time remaining: 38 seconds
```

```
$ sudo watchdogutil disarm
Watchdog disarmed successfully

$ date +%s; sudo ls -l /var/run/lock/pddf-locks/watchdog.pause
1769629534
ls: cannot access '/var/run/lock/pddf-locks/watchdog.pause': No such file or directory
```

Watchdog is re-armed by puncher eventually
```
$ date +%s; sudo watchdogutil status
1769629570
Status: Armed
Time remaining: 357 seconds
```
